issue: Ptolemaic proportional temporal position versus Regiomontanian position circles
reconciliation: Ptolemy locates contacts by relative horizon/meridian temporal position, not universal sign ascensions; Lilly names Regiomontanus but his sampled introductory passage delegates complete mathematics. Neither makes Regio position circles identical to exact proportional semi-arcs.
evidence_layer: PT Robbins English independently checked in Chicago HTML; Lilly source-annotation branch; Gansten Kindle audit secondary
implementation_implication: Separate geometry IDs; same points and key yield different arcs; no inferred historical identity.
unverified_next_check: Independent original Regiomontanus/Morin direction computation and complete Lilly examples

issue: Sign rising-time approximation and Alcabitius terminology
reconciliation: Ptolemy rejects using local sign-rising times universally and gives an explicitly approximate shortcut. This does not establish what each Valens/Paul/al-Qabisi worked algorithm meant.
evidence_layer: PT Robbins English independently checked; other traditions from Gansten audit only
implementation_implication: Separate sign-rising-time interpolation from exact semi-arc solver. Never label a program Alcabitius without its actual formula.
unverified_next_check: Original Valens/Paul/al-Qabisi examples and their tabular rise times

issue: Candidate significators versus five hylegiacal places
reconciliation: Ptolemy distinguishes eligible spatial regions and natal candidates, while Lilly identifies five hylegiacal places in a particular directions chapter and treats other directed domains elsewhere. The two five-item sets have different functions and must not be conflated.
evidence_layer: PT Robbins English independently checked; Lilly audited original annotations
implementation_implication: Two registries: allowed significator set for each technique and eligible sky-region condition for selected purposes.
unverified_next_check: Lilly general significator list and author marginal customary-five wording in full original setting

issue: Lot of Fortune day/night reversal and status as a directed point
reconciliation: Robbins III.10 main translation explicitly uses the same Sun-to-Moon direction from Ascendant by day and night, while editor notes variants. Lilly includes Fortune among five directed places, not proof that his Fortune formula follows this variant.
evidence_layer: PT Robbins English independently checked; Lilly source annotations only
implementation_implication: Keep Ptolemy fixed day/night expression and alternative sect-dependent Lot formulas as separate configurations.
unverified_next_check: Ptolemy Greek variants, other Hellenistic lots and original Lilly formula for Fortune

issue: One equinoctial degree per year versus printed Naibod conversion tables
reconciliation: Ptolemy year unit is one degree of equatorial rotation, not longitude. Lilly has a Naibod table with literal cells and internal irregularities; it cannot be replaced silently with modern exact 360/365.25 rational.
evidence_layer: PT Robbins English independently checked; Lilly source-annotation branch
implementation_implication: Parameterize a symbolic 1°/year and a modern rational-mean-solar diagnostic separately from historical printed Naibod tables.
unverified_next_check: Full 1647/1659 Naibod table second-reader cell check; Cardan/Brahe original wording
